**Message 1**

```text
gauntlet: question
One premise needs a small correction. The gather draft says jobs/report.ts sends "to reports." In the code, report(message, channel) already sends to whatever channel its caller passes (jobs/report.ts:1-2), so the requested-channel behavior already exists. The gap is that it works through a second copy of the formatting and retry loop, not through the shared helper.

Every other load-bearing premise is supported by primary code:
- lib/notify.ts#post hard-codes channel "general", formats as `[notice] ${message}`, and retries once before rethrowing (lib/notify.ts:2-6).
- jobs/report.ts repeats that template, retry count, and fetch call line for line (jobs/report.ts:2-6).
- jobs/digest.ts calls post("Daily digest") with no channel, so it depends on the general default (jobs/digest.ts:2).

No loader or runtime dependency sits on either path, so no premise is unverified. The fixture shows no caller of report() itself. I am keeping its (message, channel) signature as its public contract.

The framing holds: I checked lib/notify.ts#post and traced jobs/report.ts's inline send and jobs/digest.ts's default-channel call. Both share one formatting and retry contract, and neither depends on anything beyond fetch. Moving report onto the owning helper fixes the root cause (the duplicated loop) rather than patching around it.

How should post's existing callers stay compatible once post accepts a channel?
A) post gains an optional channel argument defaulting to "general"; existing calls are untouched
B) post requires a channel, and existing callers pass "general" explicitly
C) post stays as is, and report keeps its own send path
D) other - name it
Recommendation: A - digest keeps working unchanged, and report can delegate to the one retry loop.
```

**Message 2 (approaches, after the recorded answers)**

No implicit dependency was recorded as missing or uncheckable. Both caller paths and the helper were traced directly, and fetch is the only external call.

The two real options differ on one axis: where the "general" default lives. It can live in post's signature or at each call site. A new notification service is not an approach, since you ruled it out. Leaving report's copied loop in place is not one either: that copy is the debt this work removes.

**Recommended: optional channel on the shared helper.** post becomes post(message, channel = "general"). report() keeps its signature but its body becomes a single call to post(message, channel). Formatting and retries then live in exactly one place, and digest's default-channel call is unchanged. Changing only the owning construct is the reuse-only option. Its blast radius is limited to callers of post, and none of them change behavior.
Removes: jobs/report.ts inline body construction, `[notice]` template copy, retry loop, and fetch call
Adds: optional `channel` parameter (default "general") on lib/notify.ts#post; import of post in jobs/report.ts; report() body delegating to post(message, channel)
Pattern: follows lib/notify.ts#post as the single owning notification path and deletes the parallel copy at jobs/report.ts:2-6.

**Alternative: required channel argument.** post becomes post(message, channel), and every existing caller passes "general" explicitly. report() delegates the same way. The benefit is that no caller can silently fall into general, and the TypeScript compiler will flag every call site. The cost is the blast radius. Every caller of post has to change, which today means digest (jobs/digest.ts:2), plus any other caller in the repo. Each edit is a behavior-neutral churn line, and it adds nothing the default doesn't already guarantee.
Removes: jobs/report.ts inline body construction, template copy, retry loop, and fetch call; the implicit "general" default in post
Adds: required `channel` parameter on lib/notify.ts#post; explicit "general" argument at jobs/digest.ts:2 and every other post call site; import of post in jobs/report.ts; report() body delegating to post(message, channel)
Pattern: also consolidates onto lib/notify.ts#post. It trades a shared default for explicit routing at every caller.

I recommend the optional argument. It meets every requirement (report reaches its requested channel, retries stay in one loop, and digest keeps general) with the smallest change set.

I would switch to the required argument if the repo has, or plans, callers where landing in general by omission would be a bug. In that case, making the compiler force an explicit channel is worth the call-site churn.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
## 1. First message to the user

The framing holds: I checked the supplied `lib/notify.ts#post` implementation, traced the inline delivery path in `jobs/report.ts`, and checked `jobs/digest.ts`’s message-only call. Both delivery implementations apply `[notice]` formatting, attempt delivery twice after failures, and propagate the second failure. The shared helper currently fixes the channel to `general`; the report job duplicates that contract to accept a channel.

The fixtures support consolidating delivery in the existing helper rather than introducing a notification service. The gathered observations identify no additional loader or runtime dependency, and nothing in the supplied code contradicts that finding. There are no remaining load-bearing claims requiring an external lookup.

I’ll retain the recorded framing and compare the approved optional-channel and required-channel alternatives without another clarification question.

## 2. Approaches message

I recommend **A: an optional channel argument on the existing helper**. The distinguishing axis is caller compatibility: keep the default within the owning helper, or require every caller to choose a channel explicitly. No implicit dependency was recorded as missing or uncheckable; the supplied observations report successful tracing of both callers with no extra runtime dependency.

### A) Reuse `post` with an optional channel and preserve its default

Change the signature to `post(message: string, channel: string = "general")` and serialize that channel in the existing request body. Replace the report job’s inline delivery implementation with a call to `post(message, channel)`. Leave the digest’s message-only call unchanged.

This is the minimal reuse-only option. The shared path already provides formatting, retries, and terminal error propagation; its only missing behavior is selecting the channel. Keeping the default there preserves existing callers without another configuration path or service. Report delivery inherits future fixes to the same contract instead of maintaining a copy.

The trade-off is that omitting the channel remains valid, even for a caller that intended to supply one.

Removes: `jobs/report.ts`’s duplicated body formatting, request, retry loop, and terminal-error handling.  
Adds: a defaulted channel parameter and its payload use in `lib/notify.ts#post`; a shared-helper import and delegation in `jobs/report.ts`.  
Pattern: consolidates duplicated delivery behavior into its existing owner, `lib/notify.ts#post`, while preserving `jobs/digest.ts`’s current calling contract.

### B) Reuse `post` with a required channel argument

Change the signature to `post(message: string, channel: string)`. Delegate report delivery to that helper, and update the digest to `post("Daily digest", "general")`.

This drops the assumption that compatibility must come from an optional argument, as your recorded answer permits. Formatting and retries still have one owner, but channel selection becomes explicit at each call site. The digest retains its observed destination, though message-only calls no longer remain valid.

Its advantage is compile-time enforcement of channel selection. Its larger blast radius is that every existing caller must supply a channel; the supplied fixtures identify the digest as the affected message-only caller.

Removes: `jobs/report.ts`’s duplicated delivery implementation; the helper’s implicit default-channel calling contract.  
Adds: a required channel parameter and its payload use in `lib/notify.ts#post`; report import and delegation; an explicit `"general"` argument in `jobs/digest.ts`.  
Pattern: retains centralized delivery ownership in `lib/notify.ts#post`, but moves default-channel responsibility into callers such as `jobs/digest.ts`.

I would switch from A to B only if requiring explicit channel selection is more important than preserving existing message-only calls.
